title: Structured-output sentinel recovery and constraint-sampler evaluation playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Purpose: validate and harden JSON-mode enforcement across streaming outputs and interleaved tool/function calls using a sentinel-based recovery strategy and a probabilistic constraint-sampler. Background: previous suites focused on deterministic contract enforcement and backoff. This ticket builds a complementary playbook that intentionally injects partial/escaped tokens, interleaved tool invocations, and schema relaxations to measure recovery effectiveness, telemetry coverage, and cross-model compatibility. Goals: (1) exercise decoder-level sentinels and recovery handlers end-to-end in streaming paths; (2) evaluate a constraint-sampler that probabilistically relaxes required fields to measure graceful degradation; (3) ensure tool/function calling does not break schema guards; (4) capture telemetry to quantify repair-success-rate, schema-violation-rate, tokens-to-repair, and latency impact; (5) produce a runbook for mitigating common failure modes and a dashboard for continuous regression monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel injection harness can produce reproducible partial-emit scenarios across 5 model families (verified by CI)
Constraint-sampler exposes at least 12 unique schema-relaxation variants and produces per-variant pass/fail metrics
Recovery handler achieves >= 90% repair-success-rate on synthetic kana/latin/markdown payloads within 150 token budget
Tool/function call interleaving tests show < 1% unhandled toolcall-induced schema violations in canary traffic
Telemetry events emitted for violation, repair_start, repair_end, and repair_outcome with correlating request_id and token_offsets
Playbook and triage steps documented and reviewed by PM and Security
test_plan: Build sentinel injector that inserts invalid/partial JSON fragments at token boundaries in streaming mode
Implement constraint-sampler that randomly omits required fields, swaps types, or injects extra keys according to configurable distributions
Create interleaved toolcall harness: alternate model emits with simulated tool return tokens and verify schema gating behavior
Run cross-model matrix: 5 architectures x 3 quantization profiles x 2 sequence-length distributions
Capture detailed telemetry: token offsets, latency at repair start/end, model logits snapshot (sampling), and repair path chosen
Execute 10k synthetic sessions and compute per-scenario metrics; surface flaky cases to flaky-registry
Add CI job that runs lightweight seed set (100 sessions) on PRs touching constrained-decoder or streaming path

test_results_summary: Early runs (2k sessions) across three medium-sized models show overall repair-success-rate of 87%. Top failure modes: nested arrays with truncated trailing commas, toolcall marker loss due to prefix cache ordering, and language-specific escaping issues for non-Latin scripts. Constraint-sampler produced clear headroom: when sampler intensity was reduced (fewer required-field omissions) repair-success rose to 93% with sub-100 token repair budget. No high-severity customer-impact regressions observed in canary. Next steps: add targeted fixes for prefix caching, add language-specific escape rules, and expand run to full 10k sessions for stable baselines.
